items.content_html:
Updates the <img> srcset reference to describe the deterministic source selection algorithm from the HTML Standard, and removes "network speed" from the list of factors in the Responsive images guide.

Motivation

The HTML Standard now defines responsive image source selection normatively (whatwg/html#13183) instead of leaving it implementation-defined. The docs still said the browser picks a source "at its discretion" based on things like bandwidth, which no longer matches the spec or what browsers actually do.

Additional details

The new srcset text describes these steps:

  1. Deduplicate candidates with the same pixel density, keeping the earliest.
  2. Sort candidates by ascending pixel density.
  3. Pick the first candidate whose density is greater than or equal to Window.devicePixelRatio, or the last one if all are lower.

It also notes that the browser may pick a higher-density candidate if its image data is already available without a network request.

  • whatwg/html#13183
  • whatwg/html#13077
  • web-platform-tests/wpt#64665

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #46377
items.title: Document normative srcset image source selection

items.content_html:
Description

In separate commits, this PR:

  • Enhances the interactive example on the CSS reference page for the hyphens: property, and expands on its descriptive text to present a clearer picture of its function.
  • Deletes the nearly-identical, redundant § Example found at the bottom of the page.

Motivation

Examples which fail to clearly demonstrate the functionality being described at best leave the user no more enlightened than they were before, and at worst cause them to misunderstand (and potentially misuse) those features.

Repetitive examples that fail to demonstrate anything the user hasn't already seen waste their time and squander their attention.

Additional details

I realize the second commit may be controversial, which is why it's a separate commit. My personal opinion is that the similarities between the two examples are far too great to justify presenting both of them. Others may certainly disagree, and I don't feel strongly enough about this to press the issue.

Also, the second (deleted) example isn't precisely identical to the first, in all browsers.

In Chrome, it suffers from the same problem the other example had in all browsers (prior to the fix in my first commit): hyphens: manual; and hyphens: auto; render identically.

In Firefox, there are differences. Firefox's hyphens: auto; rendering is willing to break extreme­ly after the "ex-", whereas Chrome's is not.

Nevertheless, even in the Firefox case I feel the example is too similar to the previous one to be relevant.

Still, I am prepared to drop that commit if requested, or to replace it with an updated second example that does demonstrate the hyphens property in a way that's sufficiently novel. (I have no such example in mind, though. Suggestions welcome from anyone who feels it's an imperative.)

Firefox (left) vs. Chrome (right)

Description

Adds a new example, "Arranging items around a circle", to the Examples section of the cos() page. It places six numbered items in a ring using cos() and sin() with a radius and an item count.

Motivation

Issue #42910 asks for a real-world reason to use cos(). The page's interactive demo already moves a dot around a circle, but it doesn't explain why you would do that. This example shows a practical layout, a radial menu, and explains that each position is calculated from the radius and the number of items instead of being hard-coded.

I put it in the Examples section and left the intro unchanged, because reference page intros should stay a one-sentence summary.

Additional details

The example uses cos(), sin() and the translate property. I checked it in a browser and formatted the file with Prettier using the repo's config. The page build in this PR will show whether it renders correctly in MDN's preview.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #42910

items.content_html:
Description

  • Added pages for the following commands of the bluetooth module:
    • bluetooth.disableSimulation
    • bluetooth.handleRequestDevicePrompt
    • bluetooth.simulateAdapter
  • Added "Simulated adapter" and "The device prompt" sections to the bluetooth module landing page.

Every example was run against Chrome 155 (through ChromeDriver) with a local server. Firefox doesn't implement the bluetooth module.

Spec links

  • https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#bluetooth-disableSimulation-command
  • https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#bluetooth-handlerequestdeviceprompt-command
  • https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#bluetooth-simulateAdapter-command

Related issue

Doc issue: mdn/mdn#851

Compat quirks worth looking into:

General

  • bluetooth module spec_url. BCD's webdriver.bidi.bluetooth key points to the Permissions spec (https://www.w3.org/TR/permissions/#webdriver-bidi-module-permissions). The module page sets spec-urls: https://bluetooth.spec.whatwg.org/#bluetooth-module instead.
  • The bluetooth events. The sheet's Events tab has no bluetooth rows, so BCD has none of the module's four events, though Chrome implements them:
    • bluetooth.requestDevicePromptUpdated
    • bluetooth.gattConnectionAttempted
    • bluetooth.characteristicEventGenerated
    • bluetooth.descriptorEventGenerated

/cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update.

Chrome

  • simulateAdapter and disableSimulation. BCD shows both as partial since Chrome 140, with the note "Basic support". In my test run:
    • The simulated adapter applied to every tab, not only to the specified one.
    • simulateAdapter for a tab that already had an adapter also removed its simulated devices.
    • simulateAdapter accepted leSupported for a tab that already had an adapter (spec: invalid argument).
    • Both commands accepted an iframe's context ID (spec: invalid argument).
    • With leSupported: false, getAvailability() still resolved with true (spec: false).
  • handleRequestDevicePrompt. BCD shows full support since Chrome 140, with no note. In my test run:
    • An unknown prompt or device returned unknown error (spec: no such prompt and no such device).
    • An unknown context returned no such frame (spec: no such prompt).
    • A prompt that wasn't handled closed by itself after 0.1 to 2.3 seconds. The spec keeps it open until it's handled.
    • device was accepted with accept: false, which the spec's CDDL doesn't allow.

/cc @sadym-chromium for the compat sheet update.
items.title: [Technical review] Add BiDi bluetooth pages: `disableSimulation`, `handleRequestDevicePrompt`, `simulateAdapter`

Description

This PR adds pages for three commands of the storage module:

  • storage.setCookie
  • storage.getCookies
  • storage.deleteCookies

along with corresponding updates to the module overview page and the sidebar.

Question for the @mdn/webdriver team:

The size filter on storage.getCookies and storage.deleteCookies pages: the current description matches the output seen in Firefox 159 and Chrome 156, that is, sum of the cookie’s name and value, in bytes.

The spec describes size as

“byte length of the result of serializing stored cookie as it would be represented in a Cookie header.”

This seems to imply that theme=dark would occupy 10 bytes including the =. However, both browsers return size: 9 and also match a filter with size: 9, which is from counting only theme (5 bytes) and dark (4 bytes), and excluding =.

Should the separator count toward size, or does the spec wording need clarification to reflect the implemented behaviour?

Spec links

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-storage-setCookie
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-storage-getCookies
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-storage-deleteCookies

Related issues and pull requests

Project tracker: mdn/mdn#851

items.content_html:
Description

  • Added pages for the following commands of the network module:
    • network.addDataCollector
    • network.disownData
    • network.getData
    • network.removeDataCollector
  • Added a "Data collectors" section to the network module landing page.

Every example was run against Firefox Nightly 160 and Chrome 155 (through ChromeDriver) with a local server, and both browsers behaved the same unless noted below.

Spec links

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-addDataCollector
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-disownData
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-getData
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-removeDataCollector

Related issue

Doc issue: mdn/mdn#851

Compat quirks worth looking into:

Firefox

  • removeDataCollector collector. BCD shows the collector parameter, the command's only parameter and a required one, as unsupported, while the command is supported since Firefox 143. In my test run, Firefox removed collectors with it, and answered unknown IDs with no such network collector.
  • getData for data: URLs. For a fetch() of a data: URL, Firefox returned the URL's data as written instead of the body the page received: %5B%7B%22id%22%3A1%7D%5D for data:application/json,%5B%7B%22id%22%3A1%7D%5D, and W3siaWQiOjF9XQ== for data:application/json;base64,W3siaWQiOjF9XQ==, where the page received [{"id":1}] (seen in my test run; Chrome returned [{"id":1}] for both). BCD shows getData's data_url feature as supported since Firefox 146, with no note.

/cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update.

Chrome

  • getData and disownData versions. BCD shows both commands as supported since Chrome 126, but network.addDataCollector, without which there's no data to get or disown, and all their parameters since 140.
  • Data types:
    • BCD shows the response value of addDataCollector's dataTypes parameter as unsupported, but Chrome collected response bodies in every case of my test run.
    • BCD shows both values of disownData's dataType parameter (request and response) as unsupported, while the parameter itself is supported since 140. In my test run, Chrome released request and response bodies with disownData.
  • addDataCollector maxEncodedDataSize. BCD shows this required parameter as unsupported. In my test run, Chrome rejected 0 and values over 200000000 with invalid argument, but collected a 20,000-byte response with a maxEncodedDataSize of 10000, which the spec doesn't collect.
  • getData for a body still arriving. The spec has getData wait until the whole body has arrived. In my test run, Chrome answered getData sent after network.responseStarted, while the server was still sending the body, at once with unknown error ("No data found for resource with given identifier"). BCD shows getData as supported since 126, with no note.

/cc @sadym-chromium for the compat sheet update.
items.title: [Editorial review] Add BiDi network pages: `addDataCollector`, `disownData`, `getData`, `removeDataCollector`
